messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: DPA questions & next steps

Hi Samantha / Liam -

Thanks again for the chat today. Quick recap and the follow-ups I promised:

1) Controller vs Processor: Redwood operates as a processor under our standard DPA - we process customer-provided content to return model outputs and do not use customer data for model training unless explicitly agreed.

2) PII handling: We treat any customer-supplied personal data as Customer Data. By default we do not persist input PII beyond what is required for inference and short-term operational logs. Longer-term storage (for audit/analytics) is opt-in and can be contractually scoped.

3) Logging & retention: Default runtime logs (request metadata, small KV traces for debugging) are retained 30 days. We can provide configurable retention windows for Dedicated/Private deployments.

4) Subprocessors: I'll attach our current subprocessor list and an annotated copy of the DPA with the sections called out you asked about (controller/processor, breach notice, subprocessors).

5) Data residency: We support deployments in US and EU regions. Hosted API customers can pin RU/region for residency-sensitive workloads; Dedicated/Private give stronger guarantees.

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm whether Acme needs a contractual 48-hour breach notification (our baseline is 72 hours for hosted customers; 48 hours is negotiable for enterprise commitments).
- Let us know if you need us to produce a subprocessor-specific SOC2 report or additional evidence for any vendor.
- If legal wants tighter retention deletion SLAs (e.g., delete logs within X days of request), tell us the target and we can scope the language.

I've attached: Redwood_DPA_annotated.pdf (annotated with the items we discussed) and SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf.

I'll loop in Marissa (legal) to handle any specific redline requests - Marissa, FYI on Acme's ask re: 48-hour breach notice + data residency requirements.

Thanks -
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Ben -

Appreciate the recap and the annotated DPA. A few clarifying questions from our legal/security team before we take this into procurement:

- Can you confirm the exact retention windows you use for request logs vs. debug traces vs. full payloads (if stored)? You mentioned 30 days default - can that be shortened to 14 days as a requirement?
- For data residency: if we elect EU region, can you guarantee processing and storage will remain in EU for both active inference and backups? Any cross-border support for ops/debugging?
- Subprocessors: please share the full list (including cloud infra providers and any analytics/monitoring vendors) and confirm if Redwood provides 30 days' advance notice for any new subprocessor additions.
- Breach notification: our policy asks for 48-hour notice. You mentioned 72 hours; is 48 hours possible under an enterprise SLA?

Also, please confirm in writing that Redwood is the processor and Acme is the controller in the DPA wording.

If you can get Marissa to send a brief email confirming those items + the subprocessor CSV that would be great. We're aiming to get our counsel to sign off next week.

Thanks,
Samantha

Hi Samantha -

Thanks - answers below and attaching the subprocessor list. Marissa included for any contractual language/redlines.

- Retention windows:
  - Request metadata & runtime logs: default 30 days; we can set 14 days for hosted customers on a contractual basis or configure 14-day retention for Dedicated.
  - Debug traces / KV cache data: not persisted by default beyond the request lifecycle unless enabled for troubleshooting; when enabled we retain up to 7 days unless otherwise agreed.
  - Full payloads / customer opt-in storage: if you opt in to store inputs/outputs for analytics, retention is configurable and we will add deletion APIs and a contractual SLA.

- Data residency: For EU-region tenancy we commit to processing and storing inference data within EU-region infrastructure (primary + backups). Ops access for critical support is done via EU controls and logged; cross-border access is restricted and will be listed in the subprocessor disclosures. For Dedicated/Private we can tighten the controls further.

- Subprocessors: attached Data_Subprocessor_List.csv - includes cloud infra, monitoring, and logging partners. We provide notice of new subprocessors; standard baseline is 30 days' notice. If Acme requires 30 days written notice that's aligned with our practice; we can also include contractual right to object in limited circumstances.

- Breach notification: Our standard is 72 hours for hosted customers. For enterprise commitments we can support a 48-hour contractual SLA with mutual cooperation language and a defined contact protocol.

Confirming: Redwood operates as Processor; Acme Payments is Controller. We'll make that explicit in the DPA text.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa will share suggested DPA redlines (if any).
- I will send a DocuSign-ready DPA once legal aligns on language for breach notice & retention.

Marissa - can you weigh in on acceptable redline language for 48-hour breach notice and any additional indemnity/notify language Acme's counsel typically requests?

Thanks -
